implementation.summary: D35 adds the missing authenticated CLI parity for the existing FinOps usage, costs and budgets routes. ControlPlaneClient validates workspace and period scope, the CLI emits JSON or bounded tabular output, and real local HTTP tests cover CLI, SDK, alert scope and restart recovery without provider mocks.

security_and_recovery.journey: The candidate uses the authenticated control-plane client, rejects blank/untrimmed workspace and period values, preserves exact Decimal payloads, scopes alerts by workspace and recovers FinOps/alert/quality state after SQLite restart.
security_and_recovery.negative_paths: Blank/untrimmed FinOps scope and periods are rejected before transport; existing malformed cursor/serializer values, mixed-currency allocation, invalid forecast/budget inputs, legacy private-field exclusion and provider zero-skip assertions remain covered.
security_and_recovery.provider_scope: The real OTLP/HTTP Collector Contrib service was started from the pinned digest at the same clean source SHA and removed successfully. External Prometheus deployment, SMTP endpoint, HTTPS webhook, PostgreSQL FinOps/telemetry backend and production notification delivery remain untested.

open_cells: P12 remains in_progress, not qualified: real OTLP Collector acceptance and CLI parity do not certify external notification delivery, deployed Prometheus, PostgreSQL-backed telemetry/FinOps, broad service adoption, full browser candidate packaging or production operation.
The exact candidate browser lane is SKIP because the archive lacks @playwright/test; Node syntax is not browser qualification.
P13 remains blocked by the external secret-provider and release evidence boundary; P10 and P11 retain their in_progress ledger states and all other families retain their recorded states.
No release gate is closed; release remains NO-GO at 1/13 families and 0/10 gates.
limitations: The CLI adds listing parity only; allocation, forecast and budget evaluation remain service-level contracts rather than new public routes.
The exact candidate sandbox has no .git metadata by design; public status and git diff verification are checkout-only and are not converted into candidate PASS results.

An intermediate verify invocation from inside the sandbox correctly detected two Python cache files created by that invocation; the sandbox was cleaned and regenerated, and the final checkout-side verify passed with the manifest restored.
No hosted workflow or GitHub Actions evidence was used.
